literal: Desire, anger, delusion, of these three, the name to perish, will perish suffering.
translation: When the very names of these three—desire, anger, and delusion—are utterly destroyed, all suffering will also perish.
modern: விருப்பம், சினம், அறியாமை ஆகிய இந்த மூன்றின் பெயரும் அழியும்படி ஒழிந்தால், பிறவித்துன்பம் அழியும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the path to liberation by identifying the three root causes of all human suffering: desire (kāmam), anger (vekuḷi), and delusion or ignorance (mayakkam). The author asserts that suffering (nōy) is not merely reduced but completely eradicated when even the names or traces of these three defilements are wiped out. By using the word 'nāmam' (name), the verse emphasizes that the destruction of these vices must be so absolute that not even their memory or reputation remains in the mind. This complete purification leads to the cessation of all existential pain.
